arxiv-2205-13572.title: Clinical Dialogue Transcription Error Correction using Seq2Seq Models
arxiv-2205-13572.creator: Gayani Nanayakkara, Nirmalie Wiratunga, David Corsar, Kyle Martin, Anjana Wijekoon
arxiv-2205-13572.description: Abstract Good communication is critical to good healthcare. Clinical dialogue is a conversation between health practitioners and their patients, with the explicit goal of obtaining and sharing medical information. This information contributes to medical decision-making regarding the patient and plays a crucial role in their healthcare journey.

arxiv-2503-20621.title: The Fermi surface of RuO 2 measured by quantum oscillations
arxiv-2503-20621.creator: Zheyu Wu, Mengmeng Long, Hanyi Chen, Shubhankar Paul, Hisakazu Matsuki, Oleksandr Zheliuk, Uli Zeitler, Gang Li, Rui Zhou, Zengwei Zhu, Dave Graf, Theodore I. Weinberger, F. Malte Grosche, Yoshiteru Maeno, Alexander G. Eaton
arxiv-2503-20621.description: Abstract The metallic oxide RuO 2 has emerged as a promising altermagnet candidate, owing to reports of this material hosting antiferromagnetic ordering accompanied by a spin-split electronic band structure characteristic of time-reversal symmetry-breaking. However, recent studies have robustly questioned this scenario. Here we map the Fermi surface of pristine single-crystalline RuO 2 .

arxiv-2505-24847.title: Nematicity in iron pnictides: phase competition and emergent symmetry
arxiv-2505-24847.creator: Yiming Wang, Changle Liu, Shan Wu, Jianda Wu, Qimiao Si, Rong Yu
arxiv-2505-24847.description: Abstract The phase diagram of iron-based superconductors contains a host of electronic orders, which are intimately connected with their superconductivity. Here we analyze the fluctuations of one type of nematic order in another. Our analysis leads to an emergent U(1) symmetry at a first-order transition between a nematic phase and a C 4 C_{4} -symmetric charge-ordered phase.

arxiv-2507-18275.title: Dis-GEN: Disordered crystal structure generation
arxiv-2507-18275.creator: Martin Hoffmann Petersen*, Ruiming Zhu, Haiwen Dai, Savyasanchi Aggarwal, Nong Wei, Andy Paul Chen, Arghya Bhowmik, Juan Maria Garcia Lastra, Kedar Hippalgaonkar*
arxiv-2507-18275.description: Abstract A wide range of synthesized crystalline inorganic materials exhibit compositional disorder, where multiple atomic species partially occupy the same crystallographic site. As a result, the physical and chemical properties of such materials are dependent on how the atomic species are distributed among the corresponding symmetrical sites, making them exceptionally challenging to model using computational methods.

arxiv-2509-12819.title: Probabilities in Toy Regge models with odderons
arxiv-2509-12819.creator: M.A. Braun
arxiv-2509-12819.description: Abstract The possibi;lity of a probabilistic interpretation is studied for the Regge-Gribov model in zero dimensional transverse world (”Toy”) with interacting pomerons and odderons. It is found that the old recipe [ 1 ] , which allowed to introduce such interpretation in the model without odderons, does not work once odderons are included.

arxiv-2509-14066.title: A neuromorphic continuous soil monitoring system for precision irrigation
arxiv-2509-14066.creator: Mirco Tincani 1,2,* , Khaled Kerouch *,2 , Umberto Garlando 3 , Mattia Barezzi 3 , Alessandro Sanginario 3 , Giacomo Indiveri 2 , Chiara De Luca 1,2,†
arxiv-2509-14066.description: Abstract Sensory processing at the edge requires ultra-low power stand-alone computing technologies. This is particularly true for modern agriculture and precision irrigation systems which aim to optimize water usage by monitoring key environmental observables continuously using distributed efficient embedded processing elements.

arxiv-2510-10899.title: A Simple and Efficient One-Shot Signature Scheme
arxiv-2510-10899.creator: Andrew Huang, Vinod Vaikuntanathan
arxiv-2510-10899.description: Abstract One-shot signatures (OSS) are a powerful and uniquely quantum cryptographic primitive which allows anyone, given common reference string, to come up with a public verification key 𝗉𝗄 \mathsf{pk} and a secret signing state | 𝗌𝗄 ⟩ \ket{\mathsf{sk}} . With the secret signing state, one can produce the signature of any one message, but no more.

europmc-pmc4507317.creator: Wang ZP, Xing HL, Dong L, Zhang HY, Han CY, Wang XC, Chen QJ.

In this study, we used egg cell-specific promoters to drive the expression of Cas9 and obtained non-mosaic T1 mutants for multiple...

europmc-pmc5617631.title: Biochemical adaptations of the retina and retinal pigment epithelium support a metabolic ecosystem in the vertebrate eye.
europmc-pmc5617631.creator: Kanow MA, Giarmarco MM, Jankowski CS, Tsantilas K, Engel AL, Du J, Linton JD, Farnsworth CC, Sloat SR, Rountree A, Sweet IR, Lindsay KJ, Parker ED, Brockerhoff SE, Sadilek M, Chao JR, Hurley JB.
europmc-pmc5617631.description: Here we report multiple lines of evidence for a comprehensive model of energy metabolism in the vertebrate eye. Metabolic flux, locations of key enzymes, and our finding that glucose enters mouse and zebrafish retinas mostly through photoreceptors support a conceptually new...

europmc-pmc6105748.title: Reactive oxygen species, oxidative signaling and the regulation of photosynthesis.
europmc-pmc6105748.creator: Foyer CH.
europmc-pmc6105748.description: Reduction-oxidation (redox) reactions, in which electrons move from a donor to an acceptor, are the functional heart of photosynthesis. It is not surprising therefore that reactive oxygen species (ROS) are generated in abundance by photosynthesis, providing a plethora of redox...

pmc-10537413.title: Unraveling MYC’s Role in Orchestrating Tumor Intrinsic and Tumor Microenvironment Interactions Driving Tumorigenesis and Drug Resistance
pmc-10537413.creator: Zinab O. Doha, Rosalie C. Sears
pmc-10537413.description: The transcription factor MYC plays a pivotal role in regulating various cellular processes and has been implicated in tumorigenesis across multiple cancer types. MYC has emerged as a master regulator governing tumor intrinsic and tumor microenvironment interactions, supporting tumor progression and driving drug resistance.

pmc-10670875.title: Hair Growth Promotion and Anti-Hair Loss Effects of By-Products Arabica Coffee Pulp Extracts Using Supercritical Fluid Extraction
pmc-10670875.creator: Anurak Muangsanguan, Pichchapa Linsaenkart, Tanakarn Chaitep, Jiraporn Sangta, Sarana Rose Sommano, Korawan Sringarm, Chaiwat Arjin, Pornchai Rachtanapun, Kittisak Jantanasakulwong, Yuthana Phimolsiripol, Juan M. Castagnini, Warintorn Ruksiriwanich
pmc-10670875.description: Coffee has been a common ingredient in many traditional hair loss remedies, but limited scientific evidence supports its use, particularly in coffee pulp. Androgenetic alopecia (AGA) is caused by androgens, inflammation, and oxidative stress. In the present study, supercritical fluid extraction (SFE) was used under various conditions to obtain six coffee pulp extracts.

pmc-10689721.title: Solving complex nanostructures with ptychographic atomic electron tomography
pmc-10689721.creator: Philipp M Pelz, Sinéad M Griffin, Scott Stonemeyer, Derek Popple, Hannah DeVyldere, Peter Ercius, Alex Zettl, Mary C Scott, Colin Ophus
pmc-10689721.description: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) is essential for determining atomic scale structures in structural biology and materials science. In structural biology, three-dimensional structures of proteins are routinely determined from thousands of identical particles using phase-contrast TEM. In materials science, three-dimensional atomic structures of complex nanomaterials have been determined using atomic electron tomography (AET).

pmc-11672340.title: CD73: agent development potential and its application in diabetes and atherosclerosis
pmc-11672340.creator: Dan Liu, Jingjing Zhao, Ling Li, Jie Wang, Chao Wang, Yudong Wu, Yucun Huang, Dongming Xing, Wujun Chen
pmc-11672340.description: CD73, an important metabolic and immune escape-promoting gene, catalyzes the hydrolysis of adenosine monophosphate (AMP) to adenosine (ADO). AMP has anti-inflammatory and vascular relaxant properties, while ADO has a strong immunosuppressive effect, suggesting that CD73 has pro-inflammatory and immune escape effects. However, CD73 also decreased proinflammatory reaction, suggesting that CD73 has a positive side to the body.

pmc-11728447.title: Tympanic Pre-Operative Electrically Evoked Auditory Late Response (TympEALR) as an Alternative to Trans-Tympanic Tests Using Anesthesia in Cochlear Implant Candidacy
pmc-11728447.creator: Daniel Polterauer, Maike Neuling, Florian Simon
pmc-11728447.description: Background/Objectives: Before a cochlear implant is considered, patients undergo various audiological tests to assess their suitability. One key test measures the auditory brainstem response (ABR) to acoustic stimuli. However, in some cases, even with maximum sound stimulation, no response is detected. Methods: The promontory test involves electrical stimulation near the auditory nerve, allowing patients to associate the sensation.

pmc-12651692.title: Quality of Life and Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Skull Base Chordoma and Chondrosarcoma Treated with Pencil-Beam Scanning Proton Therapy
pmc-12651692.creator: Katarina Bryjova, Paul-Henry Mackeprang, Dominic Leiser, Damien C Weber, Sebastiano Mercadante
pmc-12651692.description: Simple SummaryUnderstanding of long-term QoL in skull base Ch and ChSa patients following PT is essential due to their relatively long survival. Previous data on this aspect was limited to only one study with a short follow-up period. Our study aims to fill this gap by providing the first analysis of QoL in these patients in a long-term follow-up setting.

pmc-12677656.title: Phospholipid Remodeling and Tri‐Layer Membrane Reconstruction Mediate Cognitive Effects of Humanized Milk Fat Globules in Neonatal Rats
pmc-12677656.creator: Shaolei Wang, Fengzhi Qiao, Jian He, Jianxin Fu, Tongjie Liu, Huaxi Yi, Qinghai Sheng, Lanwei Zhang, Kai Lin
pmc-12677656.description: Human milk fat globules (MFG) are critical for cognitive development during early life. Here, the first study is presented to simulate the phospholipid composition of human milk fat globules and reconstruct their tri‐layer membrane to evaluate their effects on cognitive function.

pmc-12712669.title: RFX1 Regulates Immune Microenvironment and Predicts Immunotherapy Response in Colon Cancer: A Multi-Omics and Clinical Analysis
pmc-12712669.creator: Zhujiang Dai, Xiaoyong Ge, Wenbo Tang, Chen-Ying Liu, Yun Liu, Zhongchuan Wang
pmc-12712669.description: ObjectiveThe plastic role of regulatory factor X1 (RFX1) in colon cancer progression and its impact on the tumor microenvironment remain poorly understood. The study aimed to clarify the molecular and clinical role of RFX1 in colon cancer.MethodsWe classified colon cancers into subgroups with high and low RFX1 expression and characterized their immune profiles, mutational profiles, cancer immunotherapy and drug sensitivity.

pmc-12736515.title: The Defense Response of Honeyberry to Root Rot Pathogens: Evidence Based on Pathogen Identification and Host Mechanism
pmc-12736515.creator: Siyu Qiao, Dianwen Wei, Hui Chen, Jinghua Yu, Shufang Gong, Zhiyong Niu, Aimin Zhou, Kun Qiao, Jingang Wang, Yanqiang Gao, Lixin Li
pmc-12736515.description: Honeyberry plants (Lonicera caerulea L., family Caprifoliaceae), which produce small, highly nutritious berries, have recently been subject to an outbreak of root rot, resulting in a drastic decrease in fruit yield. In this study, we isolated the fungal community from the roots of diseased plants and analyzed the mechanisms of interaction between key fungi and honeyberry plants.

pmc-12751871.title: Molecular regulatory network of glycolytic reprogramming in hepatocellular carcinoma and its clinical implications
pmc-12751871.creator: Hengzhou Zhu, Jiahui Li, Jiaying Zhang, Dong Niu, Weiwang Zheng, Chunhui Jin
pmc-12751871.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) ranks among the most prevalent malignant tumors worldwide, exhibiting persistently high incidence and mortality rates. Metabolic reprogramming, particularly the ‘Warburg effect’ characterized by aberrantly enhanced glycolysis, serves as a hallmark feature of HCC and various other malignancies. Even under oxygen-sufficient conditions, tumor cells preferentially utilize the glycolytic pathway to convert glucose into lactate.

pmc-12785913.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Emerging Antidepressant Strategies: From Ketamine to Neuromodulation
pmc-12785913.creator: Mateusz Kowalczyk, David Aebisher, Jakub Szpara, Sara Czech, Dorota Bartusik-Aebisher, Gabriela Henrykowska
pmc-12785913.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Depression is a common, debilitating, and potentially life-threatening mental disorder affecting individuals across all age groups and populations. It represents one of the major challenges of contemporary medicine. It is estimated that more than 300 million people worldwide are affected, and patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) exhibit a significantly increased risk of suicide, underscoring the urgent need for effective and long-lasting therapeutic strategies.

pmc-13051493.title: Streptomyces morookaense spinal suppurative infection: a case report
pmc-13051493.creator: Liyang Wu, Jiahao Pu, Xinhua Xi, Yongzhen Bao, Lincong Luo
pmc-13051493.description: PurposeStreptomyces species are ubiquitous soil actinomycetes and a major source of antibiotics, but invasive human infection with spinal involvement is exceedingly rare and may mimic tuberculous or fungal spondylodiscitis. We report a thoracic suppurative vertebral infection caused by Streptomyces morookaense and highlight an integrated diagnostic approach.

pmc-13056584.title: MedicalPhoto: Open-Source Clinical Photo Management Software for Digital Transformation
pmc-13056584.creator: Myoung Shin Kim, Sung Eun Chang, Gyeong Hoon Kim, Cristian Navarrete-Dechent, SoHyun Kim, Seong Hwan Kim, Seung Seog Han
pmc-13056584.description: e (AI) use and development, yet in many parts of the world, patient photographs are often stored on PCs without indexing, making retrieval difficult and wasting time on manual organization. We have developed a medical photographic management system, in development since 2003 and open-sourced in 2007 (MedicalPhoto; https://github.com/whria78/medicalphoto).

pmc-13219532.title: Indoor environmental factors and pneumonia in preschool children in Haikou China
pmc-13219532.creator: Shuomin Wang, Qisheng Wu, Yifan Hu, Bingxian Zhou, Shiheng Fan, Dee Yu, Zhen Yan, Jing Zhang
pmc-13219532.description: This study aims to investigate the prevalence of pneumonia in preschool children in Haikou City and assess the correlates of indoor environmental factors on this condition. A cross-sectional survey was conducted from December 2020 to January 2021. Using a stratified random sampling method, eight kindergartens in Haikou City were selected for a questionnaire-based investigation.

pmc-13306733.title: From Structural Kinematics to Thermomechanical Degradation in Polymer and Hybrid Negative Thermal Expansion Metamaterials
pmc-13306733.creator: Benjamín Méndez, Rodrigo Valle, César Garrido, Laurent Duchêne, Víctor Tuninetti
pmc-13306733.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Metamaterials with tailored structural architectures enable negative thermal expansion through geometric mechanisms that counteract constituent-level positive expansion. This study evaluates the thermomechanical performance and structural limits of polymer and hybrid NTE lattices. We systematically classify the dominant kinematic mechanisms, including bimetallic bending, rotational squares, and re-entrant honeycombs, and quantify the inherent trade-offs between effective thermal contraction, structural stiffness, and mass efficiency.

pmc-13600026.title: Nonlinear Association of Length of Stay with In-Hospital Mortality in Alzheimer’s Disease Hospitalizations: Admission-Only vs. Inpatient-Course Prediction Using Explainable Machine Learning
pmc-13600026.creator: Tursun Alkam, Ebrahim Tarshizi, Andrew H. Van Benschoten
pmc-13600026.description: Background: Hospitalizations among patients with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) carry substantial mortality risk, but length of stay (LOS) is time-dependent and may reflect heterogeneous inpatient trajectories. We examined unadjusted and adjusted LOS–mortality patterns and compared admission-only versus inpatient-course prediction using explainable machine learning.

pmc-13678119.creator: Min Niu, Xiaoming Su, Zhen Ma, Lulu Li
